actions.text: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agencies, officers, employees, broadcasters, interactive computer services, artificial intelligence system providers, and aggrieved persons or state attorneys general bringing civil actions.
dimensions.evidence: A person aggrieved by a violation of subsection (b), including an information content provider, may bring a civil action

dimensions.assessment: Creates legal liability for federal employees, allows civil suits for compensatory damages and equitable relief, and imposes mandatory reporting and transparency portals for agency communications.
dimensions.evidence: a person may obtain compensatory damages and the cost of the civil action, including reasonable attorney fees

dimensions.assessment: Involves federal indemnification of employees, potential defense costs by the Department of Justice, and costs for establishing NIST standards, an OSTP portal, and public websites.
dimensions.evidence: the Federal Government shall indemnify the officer or employee for any verdict, judgment, or other monetary award rendered against the officer or employee.

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Communications Act of 1934, the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act, and the National Science and Technology Policy, Organization, and Priorities Act of 1976.
dimensions.evidence: Title VII of the Communications Act of 1934 (47 U.S.C. 601 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent statutory prohibitions, ongoing biennial updates to standards, and recurring reporting requirements.
dimensions.evidence: Not less than once every 2 years, the Director shall... review the standards and guidelines

missing_information: Exact figures on the cost of establishing and maintaining the portal and website are not provided.
The precise number of federal communications that will be logged and reviewed annually is not specified.
importance_detail.rationale: The JAWBONE Act creates a new federal cause of action and private right of action regarding federal agency communications with broadcasters, interactive computer services, and AI providers, along with new NIST standards and an OSTP portal.
